identity.metric: speechbrain ECAPA cosine on 16 kHz neutral clips
identity.criterion: every pairwise neutral cosine is at or below the maximum real AMI same-gender between-speaker cosine
identity.note: The criterion is permissive and uses the observed real maximum. The Timothee/Jackie pair is in the upper tail of the real between-speaker distribution; see the percentile column.

identity_preservation.metric: ECAPA cosine to the same voice's neutral clip
identity_preservation.criterion: every emotion and accent clip stays at or above ECAPA cosine 0.90 to that voice's neutral clip
identity_preservation.note: The 0.90 floor is a pre-declared identity-preservation guard, not a human similarity judgment. The rejected sad pitch shift failed it.

emotion.note: Direction checks are measured on the generated demo clips. They verify the intended prosodic direction, not perceptual recognition. Happy and angry are checked for higher F0 and shorter duration. Sad is checked for longer duration only: the E1 sad F0 lowering did not transfer to the calibrated face styles, and a post-synthesis pitch shift collapsed speaker identity, so it was not used.

emotion_application.criterion: all expected clips present; each condition changes the style away from the calibrated neutral style; condition styles are pairwise distinct per voice; ECAPA-to-neutral >= 0.90
emotion_application.note: This verifies condition application and identity preservation. It does not establish perceptual emotion or accent recognition.

accent.note: The A3 classifier was trained on real GLOBE features and its generated-audio proxy is weak. No human accent-identification study exists. The three accents are applied conditions, not validated perceptual accents.

accent_application.criterion: all expected clips present; each condition changes the style away from the calibrated neutral style; condition styles are pairwise distinct per voice; ECAPA-to-neutral >= 0.90
accent_application.note: This verifies condition application and identity preservation. It does not establish perceptual emotion or accent recognition.

mos.reason: no human MOS/CMOS ratings were collected

limitations: No human MOS, CMOS, emotion-identification, or accent-identification study was run.
The three voices are face-derived embedding identities, not claims about the people in the images.
The style-manifold calibration is an exploratory demo transform, not a serving path.

Emotion scale 0.56 is twice the E1-validated 0.28. The E1 sad F0 lowering did not transfer to the calibrated face styles; a post-synthesis pitch shift was tested and rejected because it collapsed ECAPA identity to about 0.57. Sad is therefore carried by its duration change only.
Happy and angry share a similar F0 rise; angry is separated mainly by a larger duration reduction. Perceptual distinctness is not established.
Accent scale 1.0 is above the A3-selected 0.3; the A3 classifier gain was one clip and per-class recall was weak for US and Australian.
The N1 LoRA is omitted because the controlled matrix showed worse noise than the calibrated baseline.
The Timothee/Jackie neutral identity pair is in the upper tail of the real AMI between-speaker distribution.
WER is an ASR proxy and is not a naturalness or intelligibility rating.
